Below is a structured 12-week postpartum return-to-training plan tailored for a 33-year-old woman, 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section, cleared for light activity (walking, no abs, no heavy lifting, no jumping) until six-week check. This plan progresses cautiously from gentle mobility and basic core re-activation to more strength and conditioning, staying within safe postpartum guidelines. It uses only a yoga mat and bodyweight, with optional resistance bands later if provided by the client. Always monitor any signs of pain, diastasis recti, or pelvic floor issues and adjust accordingly. Obtain medical clearance if any red flags arise (incontinence with activity, pelvic floor pain, heavy bleeding, or persistent abdominal separation).

Goals by week 12
- Core: re-engage deep abdominal muscles, progressively restore bracing and functional core strength.
- Pelvic floor: improve tone and coordination; ensure no leakage with light activities as appropriate.
- Mobility: normalize hip/ thoracic spine mobility; restore diastasis safely with progressive breathing.
- Strength: introduce foundational upper/lower body movements with proper tempo and technique.
- Conditioning: build gentle cardiovascular capacity via walking and low-impact work.
- Recovery: emphasize sleep, nutrition, hydration, and progressive load management.

Important notes about diastasis recti and pelvic floor
- Do not perform any crunches, sit-ups, V-ups, or movements that dome the abdomen early on.
- Focus on abdominal wall bracing (transverse abdominis activation) with diaphragmatic breathing.
- If any abdominal dome, bulge, or leakage occurs, regress and consult a clinician.
- Pelvic floor: avoid high-impact or heavy lifting; perform gentle pelvic floor activation and coughing exercises with proper breath.

Program structure
- Weekly format: 3–4 days of movement per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat or Tue/Thu/Sat). 30–45 minutes per session initially, progressing to 45–60 minutes.
- Phases: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4, early reintroduction), Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8, progressive loading and core activation), Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12, strength and conditioning with controlled intensity).
- Warm-up: 5–7 minutes each session (gentle mobility, breathing, light activation).
- Cool-down: 5 minutes with gentle stretches and breathing.
- Progression criteria: only advance to next phase when technique is solid, no pelvic floor issues, and energy levels allow.

Phase 0/Preparatory checks (weeks 0–1)
- If you’re already at week 4 post-C-section, treat Week 1 as a re-entry week focusing on body awareness, diaphragmatic breathing, and establishing a daily movement habit without loading.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — reintroduction and diaphragmatic core activation
Objective: Reconnect with diaphragmatic breathing, activate transverse abdominis and pelvic floor, restore hip mobility, begin gentle lower-body work with no load.

Session structure: 3 days/week (adjust days as needed)
- Warm-up (5–7 minutes): diaphragmatic breathing in supine or hands-kace, pelvic floor activation, gentle cat-camel, hip circles.
- Main work (20–25 minutes): low-load moves focusing on form.
- Cool-down (5 minutes): gentle hamstring/hip flexor stretches, plus breathing.

Core and pelvic floor activation exercises (begin with 1 set, 8–10 reps or time-based):
- Breath work: diaphragmatic breathing 4-6 breaths per side lying or seated.
- Transverse abdominal activation (TA brace): lying supine with knees bent, place one hand under small of back; with exhale gently draw the lower abdomen toward spine without neck tension; hold 3 seconds, release. Do 6–8 reps, 2 sets.
- Pelvic floor activation: gentle Kegels (short/long holds) 2–3 sets of 5–8 reps; progress to longer holds if no pelvic pressure.
- Glute activation: glute bridges with marching (bridge 2–3 sets of 8–10 reps, with optional light toe taps to keep core braced) or seated band-resisted leg extensions if available.
- Scapular mobility: wall slides with light scapular engagement (standing, arms on wall, slide up and down 6–8 reps) to improve posture.

Low-impact lower body moves (no loading or impact):
- Standing hip hinge to chair or wall (modified deadlift pattern with no weight): 2 sets of 8–10 reps, focusing on neutral spine and TA activation.
- Side-lying clamshells: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps per side using no resistance or light resistance band if available.
- Supine pelvic tilt and leg extension progressions: 2–3 sets of 8–10 reps.

Breathing and brace cues:
- Exhale on exertion; maintain rib cage down and pelvis braced during every movement.
- Avoid dome or bulge in the midline; keep abdomen "soft and braced" without bearing down.

Optional progression to Week 2–4:
- If no discomfort and technique solid, gradually increase reps to 12 per set or add 1 extra set for each exercise so long as the client can complete with good form.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 — progressive core activation and light strength
Objective: Build core endurance, begin light resistance with bands or light bodyweight, reintroduce loading in a controlled way, increase walking time and intensity.

Session structure: 3 days/week
- Warm-up (7 minutes): dynamic hip flexor/hamstring mobility, ankle mobility, and shoulder warm-up.
- Core and pelvic floor: TA activation, diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor, and gentle anti-extension/core stability work.
- Strength work: begin to introduce light resistance or more challenging bodyweight movements.
- Conditioning: end with a 5–10 minute brisk walk or light cardio if energy allows.
- Cool-down: 5–7 minutes of mobility and stretch.

Core/anti-extension exercises (4–5 exercises, 2–3 sets, 10–12 reps or 20–30 seconds holds):
- Modified dead bug (contralateral limb extension with brace): keep lower back pressed to floor; avoid arching.
- Pallof press with resistance band (standing or kneeling): 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps per side; controlled line of pull.
- Bird-dog (on all fours, opposite arm and leg extension): aim for 2–3 sets of 8–10 reps per side; maintain neutral spine.
- Dead bug with small ball squeeze between knees (if available): 2–3 sets of 8–10 reps.
- Glute bridges with hold: 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps with 2–3 second hold at top; progress to a single-leg bridge if capable.

Lower body strengthening (no heavy load or impact):

Great question. Reintroducing core work safely after clearance (especially postpartum, with prior C-section and diastasis considerations) hinges on three pillars: gradual loading, thorough bracing/breathing, and close monitoring for signs of diastasis or pelvic floor stress. Here’s a practical, step-by-step approach you can use with your client.

Guiding principles
- Start with the deepest core: transverse abdominis (TA) bracing with diaphragmatic breathing, not with traditional “core” crunches.
- Progress load only when technique is flawless and no abdominal bulge or pelvic floor symptoms appear.
- Prioritize pelvic floor coordination: maintain gentle activation throughout all movements; avoid bearing down or Valsalva.
- Use a controlled tempo and avoid ballistic or high-impact movements until fully prepared.
- Monitor symptoms daily; if any dome/bulge, leakage, pelvic pressure, or unusual pain occurs, regress immediately.

Baseline assessment (before reintroducing loaded core)
- Diaphragmatic breathing check: client can inhale deeply into the abdomen and lower ribcage, then exhale with a gentle 3–4 second exhale while maintaining abdominal bracing.
- TA bracing cue: in supine with knees bent, place one hand under the lower back; on exhale, feel the belly draw toward the spine without flattening the back into the mat. Maintain 3–5 seconds brace.
- Pelvic floor awareness: Kegel cues (short holds, then longer holds) integrated with breath; ensure no pelvic heaviness or leakage during light activation.
- Diastasis check (non-clinical): client can perform a gentle transverse brace while performing a dead bug or toe tap; if there is bulging or doming with any rep, stop and regress.

Progression framework for core work (weeks 7–12, no jumping)
Phase A: Reconnect and build endurance (Weeks 7–8)
- Focus: anti-extension control, anti-rotation control, breathing coordination.
- Exercises (2–3 sets, 10–12 reps or 20–30 seconds holds):
  - Dead bug with full brace: opposite arm/leg moving while the lower back stays pressed to the floor.
  - Half-kneeling Pallof press (light resistance band): control line of pull; resist rotation without trunk collapse.
  - Bird-dog (neutral spine, slow tempo): 2–3 seconds per phase; avoid rocking pelvis.
  - Side planks (knees down): hold 15–25 seconds, progress to full side plank as tolerated.
- Progression cues: increase hold times by 5–10 seconds or increase reps, only when no rib flare or doming occurs.

Phase B: Anti-rotation and endurance with light load (Weeks 9–10)
- Add small external loads if technique is solid and diastasis signs remain stable.
- Exercises (2–4 sets, 10–15 reps or 20–30 seconds holds):
  - Pallof press with moderate resistance.
  - Anti-rotation chop via resistance band (standing, both sides) with slow controlled tempo.
  - Cable-length dead bugs or medicine-ball transitions if available (low resistance).
  - Side planks with knee/foot variation depending on tolerance; gradually extend hold time.
- Cues: maintain ribcage down, avoid shifting hips, exhale on exertion, no breath-holding.

Phase C: Integrated core stability with controlled loading (Weeks 11–12)
- Introduce light dynamic core tasks that integrate with total-body movements:
  - Farmer’s carry with light dumbbells or clusters with a focus on bracing (if allowed by clinician and diastasis status).
  - Renegade rows from the floor or incline; if too challenging, stick with supported rows.
  - Anti-rotation Pallof press with longer holds or tempo variations.
  - Slow tempo compound movements that require core bracing (e.g., goblet squat with a light hold at chest, braced, before lifting).
- Monitoring: ensure no abdominal dome; if any signs appear, revert to Phase A or even more basic TA/diaphragm work for a week.

General exercise selection and cues
- Prefer front-loaded/core-bracing cues: “brace around your midsection as if you’re about to be punched, but keep breathing.” Exhale during the hardest portion of the movement.
- Breathing tempo: inhale through the nose to prepare, exhale through the mouth during the difficult portion, keeping the ribcage down.
- Avoid belly-dreathing (bear down) during any core exercise; if you sense a bulge or pelvic floor stress, regress immediately.

Programming integration with the overall plan
- Allocate 2–3 dedicated core sessions per week, integrated into full-body workouts if you’re doing three weekly sessions (e.g., 2 core-focused sets at the start of the workout, then the main movement blocks).
- If she’s cleared for more total-workload but you want to ensure diastasis safety, structure core work as a separate block at the start of the workout and separate from high-load lifting days.
- Combine with pelvic floor checks: after each week, reassess symptoms (bulge, leakage, fatigue). If any negative signs appear, revert to a safer, earlier phase core work.

Progression decision rules
- Move from Phase A to Phase B only if:
  - No diastasis bulge during dead bugs and Pallof presses.
  - Pelvic floor remains stable with light activation during all reps.
  - She reports no increased abdominal or pelvic floor pain post-workout.
- Move to Phase C only if:
  - Able to maintain core bracing and technique under increased loads without signs of doming or leakage.
  - Energy and recovery are consistently good, and clinician signs off on progression.

Practical tips for you as the trainer
- Use a simple progression log: phase, exercise, sets, reps, load, symptom checks (bulge, leakage, pain) after each session.
- Keep observation cues: watch for rib flare, pelvis tilt, and any compensatory patterns (excess spinal extension, shoulder or neck tension).
- Maintain coupling with breathing: ensure every core exercise emphasizes exhale on exertion.
- If you have access to a clipboard and a small form, create a one-page “core reintroduction protocol” that you can hand to the client for home practice.

Here is a fully consolidated 12-week postpartum plan, integrating all prior adjustments (4 weeks post-C-section, phase progression, no jumping until after the no-jump window, breastfeeding nutrition context, and safe core reintroduction). The plan assumes 3 days/week of training initially, with an optional 4th day if energy and recovery permit. It uses only bodyweight and very light bands/equipment if available. Always prioritize form, diaphragm breathing, and pelvic floor coordination; regress if any signs of diastasis bulge, leakage, or pelvic/pelvic-floor pain appear.

Overall structure by phases
- Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — reintroduction, diaphragmatic breathing, TA activation, very light strength with no loading
- Phase 2: Weeks 5–6 — continued light loading and core work, readiness for progression
- Phase 3: Weeks 7–12 — no jumping; progressive loading with non-jumping modalities; build strength and endurance
- Phase 4 (optional planning after week 12): assess for gradual return to higher-load, higher-intensity programs or introduce controlled jumping if clearance is confirmed and symptoms remain stable

Important safety notes that run throughout
- No crunches, sit-ups, V-ups, or movements that dome the abdomen early on.
- Maintain transverse abdominis bracing with diaphragmatic breathing during all movements.
- Pelvic floor: gentle activation through all lifts; avoid bearing down or Valsalva.
- If any abdominal bulge, leakage, pelvic pressure, pain, or dizziness occurs, regress to a prior phase.
- If red flags arise (heavy bleeding, severe pain, incontinence with activity), pause and seek medical advice.

Week-by-week plan with exercises, sets, reps, and progression cues

Weeks 1–4: Phase 1 — Reintroduction and diaphragmatic core activation
Goal: Establish breathing, TA activation, pelvic floor engagement; introduce safe, low-load movements.

Weekly schedule suggestion: 3 sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat). Each session 20–40 minutes; warm-up 5–7 minutes, main work 12–25 minutes, cool-down 5 minutes.

Week 1
- Warm-up (5–7 minutes)
  - Diaphragmatic breathing: 4–6 breaths per side, seated or supine
  - Pelvic floor activation: gentle Kegels, 2–3 sets of 5–8 reps with light holds
  - Cat-camel, hip circles (spine/hips)
- Main work (1 set per exercise; 8–10 reps; no load)
  - Glute bridges with marching
  - Standing hip hinge to chair (neutral spine)
  - Side-lying clamshells (no resistance)
  - Supine pelvic tilt with leg extensions
  - Wall slides (6–8 reps)
  - Bird-dog (on all fours; 6–8 reps per side)
- Cool-down (5 minutes)
  - Gentle hamstring/hip flexor stretches; 1–2 breathing cycles
- Cues: Exhale on exertion; rib cage down; pelvis braced; avoid rib flare

Week 2
- Same structure; aim to complete 1–2 sets for select exercises if technique remains solid
- Progression: add 1 extra set to glute bridges with marching or wall slides if comfortable

Week 3
- Increase to 2 sets per exercise for the core/hip glute pattern:
  - Glute bridges with marching: 2 sets
  - Standing hip hinge to chair: 2 sets
  - Side-lying clamshells: 2 sets per side
  - Bird-dog: 2 sets per side
- Optional tiny progression: if tolerated, add a very light tempo (2 seconds down, 1 second pause, 2 seconds up) to a few reps
- Core cueing remains: exhale on exertion, keep rib cage down, brace

Week 4
- 2 sets per exercise across the board; add small top-end holds
  - Glute bridges with marching: 2 sets of 10–12 reps
  - Wall squats to chair: 2 sets of 8–12 reps
  - Goblet cue without weight (pretend-to-hold a weight): 2 sets of 8–12 reps
  - Bird-dog: 2 sets of 8–10 per side
- Core-focused progressions: maintain TA brace, add 1–2 seconds hold at top of glute bridge if tolerating
- Cardio: 20–30 minutes walking on most days; light mobility work

Weeks 5–6: Phase 2 — progressive core activation and light resistance (still no jumps)
Goal: Build core endurance; introduce light bands or light dumbbells; increase walking time.

Weeks 5–6 structure (3 days/week)
- Warm-up (6–8 minutes): dynamic hip flexor/hamstring mobility, ankle mobility, shoulder warm-up, diaphragmatic breathing
- Core/anti-extension work (3–4 exercises; 2–3 sets; 10–12 reps or 20–30 seconds holds):
  - Dead bug (braced) with contralateral limb movement
  - Pallof press (light resistance band; kneeling or standing)
  - Bird-dog (neutral spine; slower tempo)
  - Side planks (knees down initially; progress to full side plank as tolerated)
- Lower body (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Goblet squats or bodyweight squats with anterior loading cue
  - Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells or bands
  - Step-back or static lunges; control
  - Glute bridges with tempo; top hold 1–2 seconds
- Upper body (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Incline push-ups or wall push-ups
  - Bent-over rows with resistance band or light dumbbells
  - Seated or standing shoulder taps with light resistance (scapular stability)
- Conditioning (optional; no jumping)
  - Walk 30–45 minutes; one day with 15–20 minutes of intervals (2 minutes steady, 1 minute brisk)

Weeks 7–8: Phase 2 continuation — no jumping, ramp load modestly
Goal: Increase loading tolerance; deepen core stability under light resistance.

Weeks 7–8 structure (3 days/week)
- Warm-up (6–8 minutes)
- Core/anti-extension and anti-rotation (3–4 exercises; 2–3 sets; 10–15 reps or 20–30 seconds holds):
  - Dead bug progressions with light resistance
  - Pallof press (moderate resistance)
  - Bird-dog (slower tempo)
  - Side planks (progress hold time)
- Lower body strength (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Goblet squats with light hold (or bodyweight)
  - Romanian deadlift with light-to-moderate dumbbell/band
  - Step-back box step-downs; controlled
  - Glute bridges with tempo; 12–15 reps
- Upper body strength (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Incline push-ups
  - Rows with band or dumbbells
  - Seated press or shoulder taps with light resistance
- Conditioning (non-jumping)
  - Walk 30–45 minutes; add one longer day 45–60 minutes if energy permits
  - Optional low-impact circuit: 20–30 seconds work, 30 seconds rest; 4–6 rounds; moves like bodyweight squats, hip hinges, incline push-ups, rows

Weeks 9–12: Phase 3 — no jumping; progressive strength with controlled intensity
Goal: Full-body strength with gradual progression, maintain no-jump constraint, and build conditioning with low-impact intervals.

Weeks 9–10 structure (3–4 days/week)
- Warm-up (8 minutes): mobility and activation
- Main strength blocks (2–3 sets per exercise; 6–10 reps; moderate control)
  - Squats: goblet squats progressing to light dumbbell squats if tolerated
  - Romanian deadlift: light-to-moderate dumbbells or bands
  - Lunges: reverse or static lunges; controlled tempo
  - Hip thrusts/glute bridges: added load (weight plate or heavier dumbbell)
  - Push-ups: incline progressing to floor push-ups as tolerated
  - Rows: banded or dumbbell rows
  - Pallof press: 2–3 sets per side
- Conditioning: 5–10 minutes of low-impact cardio or intervals (no jumps)
- Cool-down: mobility and breath work

Weeks 11–12 structure (3–4 days/week)
- Strength emphasis: 3–4 days/week; add slight overload or tempo variation
  - Squats: goblet squats with light-moderate weight
  - Hip thrusts/glute bridges with added load
  - Romanian deadlift with heavier dumbbells/bands
  - Lunges: reverse lunges with light load
  - Push-ups: incline to floor as tolerated
  - Rows: heavier band or dumbbells
  - Pallof press variations and anti-rotation drills
- Conditioning: 1–2 days of low-impact cardio; short intervals (30–45 seconds) at brisk pace with longer recovery
- Core work: integrated as a block at the start or integrated into the workout, using the Phase A–C progression if needed:
  - Phase A (Weeks 11–12): dead bug variations, Pallof press, bird-dog; 2–3 sets; 10–15 reps or 20–30 seconds holds
  - Phase B (Weeks 11–12): anti-rotation chops or Pallof progressions
- Jumping: avoid until the clinician confirms clearance beyond 12 weeks or within a no-jump window if previously indicated; reassess with clinician before reintroducing jumping

Breastfeeding nutrition and recovery reminders (integrated)
- Protein target: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day; include protein with every meal
- Caloric target: approx 300–500 kcal/day above baseline needs (adjust for hunger, weight trajectory, milk production)
- Hydration: 2.5–3 liters/day; more on exercise days
- Micronutrients: iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc, magnesium; continue prenatal/postnatal supplementation as advised
- Caffeine: limit to 200–300 mg/day
- Post-workout: have a protein-rich snack within 60–90 minutes

Progression cues and safety checkpoints
- Core progression: only advance to the next core phase when technique is flawless, no diastasis bulge during core moves, and pelvic floor remains calm during all reps
- Load progression: increase resistance or load only if form and stability are intact; prioritize slow tempo, controlled ROM, and minimal fatigue during reps
- No jumping constraint: strictly adhere to no jumping until clinician approves; if allowed in the future, reintroduce with a planned, gradual progression

- A simple 1-page client take-home plan summarizing Week 1–12, with daily cues and a space to record symptoms

Here is a fully consolidated 12-week postpartum plan, integrating all prior adjustments (4 weeks post-C-section, phase progression, no jumping until after the no-jump window, breastfeeding nutrition context, and safe core reintroduction). The plan assumes 3 days/week of training initially, with an optional 4th day if energy and recovery permit. It uses only bodyweight and very light bands/equipment if available. Always prioritize form, diaphragm breathing, and pelvic floor coordination; regress if any signs of diastasis bulge, leakage, or pelvic/pelvic-floor pain appear.

Overall structure by phases
- Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — reintroduction, diaphragmatic breathing, TA activation, very light strength with no loading
- Phase 2: Weeks 5–6 — continued light loading and core work, readiness for progression
- Phase 3: Weeks 7–12 — no jumping; progressive loading with non-jumping modalities; build strength and endurance
- Phase 4 (optional planning after week 12): assess for gradual return to higher-load, higher-intensity programs or introduce controlled jumping if clearance is confirmed and symptoms remain stable

Important safety notes that run throughout
- No crunches, sit-ups, V-ups, or movements that dome the abdomen early on.
- Maintain transverse abdominis bracing with diaphragmatic breathing during all movements.
- Pelvic floor: gentle activation through all lifts; avoid bearing down or Valsalva.
- If any abdominal bulge, leakage, pelvic pressure, pain, or dizziness occurs, regress to a prior phase.
- If red flags arise (heavy bleeding, severe pain, incontinence with activity), pause and seek medical advice.

Week-by-week plan with exercises, sets, reps, and progression cues

Weeks 1–4: Phase 1 — Reintroduction and diaphragmatic core activation
Goal: Establish breathing, TA activation, pelvic floor engagement; introduce safe, low-load movements.

Weekly schedule suggestion: 3 sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat). Each session 20–40 minutes; warm-up 5–7 minutes, main work 12–25 minutes, cool-down 5 minutes.

Week 1
- Warm-up (5–7 minutes)
  - Diaphragmatic breathing: 4–6 breaths per side, seated or supine
  - Pelvic floor activation: gentle Kegels, 2–3 sets of 5–8 reps with light holds
  - Cat-camel, hip circles (spine/hips)
- Main work (1 set per exercise; 8–10 reps; no load)
  - Glute bridges with marching
  - Standing hip hinge to chair (neutral spine)
  - Side-lying clamshells (no resistance)
  - Supine pelvic tilt with leg extensions
  - Wall slides (6–8 reps)
  - Bird-dog (on all fours; 6–8 reps per side)
- Cool-down (5 minutes)
  - Gentle hamstring/hip flexor stretches; 1–2 breathing cycles
- Cues: Exhale on exertion; rib cage down; pelvis braced; avoid rib flare

Week 2
- Same structure; aim to complete 1–2 sets for select exercises if technique remains solid
- Progression: add 1 extra set to glute bridges with marching or wall slides if comfortable

Week 3
- Increase to 2 sets per exercise for the core/hip glute pattern:
  - Glute bridges with marching: 2 sets
  - Standing hip hinge to chair: 2 sets
  - Side-lying clamshells: 2 sets per side
  - Bird-dog: 2 sets per side
- Optional tiny progression: if tolerated, add a very light tempo (2 seconds down, 1 second pause, 2 seconds up) to a few reps
- Core cueing remains: exhale on exertion, keep rib cage down, brace

Week 4
- 2 sets per exercise across the board; add small top-end holds
  - Glute bridges with marching: 2 sets of 10–12 reps
  - Wall squats to chair: 2 sets of 8–12 reps
  - Goblet cue without weight (pretend-to-hold a weight): 2 sets of 8–12 reps
  - Bird-dog: 2 sets of 8–10 per side
- Core-focused progressions: maintain TA brace, add 1–2 seconds hold at top of glute bridge if tolerating
- Cardio: 20–30 minutes walking on most days; light mobility work

Weeks 5–6: Phase 2 — progressive core activation and light resistance (still no jumps)
Goal: Build core endurance; introduce light bands or light dumbbells; increase walking time.

Weeks 5–6 structure (3 days/week)
- Warm-up (6–8 minutes): dynamic hip flexor/hamstring mobility, ankle mobility, shoulder warm-up, diaphragmatic breathing
- Core/anti-extension work (3–4 exercises; 2–3 sets; 10–12 reps or 20–30 seconds holds):
  - Dead bug (braced) with contralateral limb movement
  - Pallof press (light resistance band; kneeling or standing)
  - Bird-dog (neutral spine; slower tempo)
  - Side planks (knees down initially; progress to full side plank as tolerated)
- Lower body (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Goblet squats or bodyweight squats with anterior loading cue
  - Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells or bands
  - Step-back or static lunges; control
  - Glute bridges with tempo; top hold 1–2 seconds
- Upper body (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Incline push-ups or wall push-ups
  - Bent-over rows with resistance band or light dumbbells
  - Seated or standing shoulder taps with light resistance (scapular stability)
- Conditioning (optional; no jumping)
  - Walk 30–45 minutes; one day with 15–20 minutes of intervals (2 minutes steady, 1 minute brisk)

Weeks 7–8: Phase 2 continuation — no jumping, ramp load modestly
Goal: Increase loading tolerance; deepen core stability under light resistance.

Weeks 7–8 structure (3 days/week)
- Warm-up (6–8 minutes)
- Core/anti-extension and anti-rotation (3–4 exercises; 2–3 sets; 10–15 reps or 20–30 seconds holds):
  - Dead bug progressions with light resistance
  - Pallof press (moderate resistance)
  - Bird-dog (slower tempo)
  - Side planks (progress hold time)
- Lower body strength (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Goblet squats with light hold (or bodyweight)
  - Romanian deadlift with light-to-moderate dumbbell/band
  - Step-back box step-downs; controlled
  - Glute bridges with tempo; 12–15 reps
- Upper body strength (2–3 sets; 8–12 reps)
  - Incline push-ups
  - Rows with band or dumbbells
  - Seated press or shoulder taps with light resistance
- Conditioning (non-jumping)
  - Walk 30–45 minutes; add one longer day 45–60 minutes if energy permits
  - Optional low-impact circuit: 20–30 seconds work, 30 seconds rest; 4–6 rounds; moves like bodyweight squats, hip hinges, incline push-ups, rows

Weeks 9–12: Phase 3 — no jumping; progressive strength with controlled intensity
Goal: Full-body strength with gradual progression, maintain no-jump constraint, and build conditioning with low-impact intervals.

Weeks 9–10 structure (3–4 days/week)
- Warm-up (8 minutes): mobility and activation
- Main strength blocks (2–3 sets per exercise; 6–10 reps; moderate control)
  - Squats: goblet squats progressing to light dumbbell squats if tolerated
  - Romanian deadlift: light-to-moderate dumbbells or bands
  - Lunges: reverse or static lunges; controlled tempo
  - Hip thrusts/glute bridges: added load (weight plate or heavier dumbbell)
  - Push-ups: incline progressing to floor push-ups as tolerated
  - Rows: banded or dumbbell rows
  - Pallof press: 2–3 sets per side
- Conditioning: 5–10 minutes of low-impact cardio or intervals (no jumps)
- Cool-down: mobility and breath work

Weeks 11–12 structure (3–4 days/week)
- Strength emphasis: 3–4 days/week; add slight overload or tempo variation
  - Squats: goblet squats with light-moderate weight
  - Hip thrusts/glute bridges with added load
  - Romanian deadlift with heavier dumbbells/bands
  - Lunges: reverse lunges with light load
  - Push-ups: incline to floor as tolerated
  - Rows: heavier band or dumbbells
  - Pallof press variations and anti-rotation drills
- Conditioning: 1–2 days of low-impact cardio; short intervals (30–45 seconds) at brisk pace with longer recovery
- Core work: integrated as a block at the start or integrated into the workout, using the Phase A–C progression if needed:
  - Phase A (Weeks 11–12): dead bug variations, Pallof press, bird-dog; 2–3 sets; 10–15 reps or 20–30 seconds holds
  - Phase B (Weeks 11–12): anti-rotation chops or Pallof progressions
- Jumping: avoid until the clinician confirms clearance beyond 12 weeks or within a no-jump window if previously indicated; reassess with clinician before reintroducing jumping

Breastfeeding nutrition and recovery reminders (integrated)
- Protein target: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day; include protein with every meal
- Caloric target: approx 300–500 kcal/day above baseline needs (adjust for hunger, weight trajectory, milk production)
- Hydration: 2.5–3 liters/day; more on exercise days
- Micronutrients: iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc, magnesium; continue prenatal/postnatal supplementation as advised
- Caffeine: limit to 200–300 mg/day
- Post-workout: have a protein-rich snack within 60–90 minutes

Progression cues and safety checkpoints
- Core progression: only advance to the next core phase when technique is flawless, no diastasis bulge during core moves, and pelvic floor remains calm during all reps
- Load progression: increase resistance or load only if form and stability are intact; prioritize slow tempo, controlled ROM, and minimal fatigue during reps
- No jumping constraint: strictly adhere to no jumping until clinician approves; if allowed in the future, reintroduce with a planned, gradual progression

Optional documentation and tools
- A weekly core progression tracker (Phase A–C with weeks) to document reps, loads, and any signs of doming or leakage
- A simple 1-page client take-home plan summarizing Week 1–12, with daily cues and a space to record symptoms
- A no-jump progression checklist to guide decision-making if the clinician later lifts the restriction
